title: Cuju, ancient Chinese football
summary: The FIFA Museum says the first recorded references to cuju, a Chinese ball game played with the feet, occur in the third century BC in Linzi, then the capital of the state of Qi. China Story says it served as fitness training for military cavaliers in the Warring States period and spread to royal courts under the Han.

as_recorded.value: the first recorded references to cuju in Chinese literature occur in the third century BC
During the Warring States Period (476-221 BC), Cuju was used as fitness training for military cavaliers.

where.historical_name: Linzi, capital of the state of Qi in the Warring States period

importance.justification: Cuju is among the earliest documented ball games played with the feet.

sources.title: Cuju, the forerunner of modern soccer
sources.author: CITS

reviewer_note: The date is when the game is first mentioned in surviving texts, not when it began. The FIFA Museum page names Linzi as the place of the earliest references; the game may be older.
